concept: Light raiding battalions for hit-and-withdraw strikes on lines of communication, from Darby's Rangers to the Korean War Ranger companies.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Long Range Patrols
concept: Six-man teams observing deep behind enemy lines for days, the Vietnam LRRP and Recondo model and the Soviet and British long-range surveillance patrols of the Central Front.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Jungle Warfare Scouts
concept: Small unit trackers who out-patrol guerrillas in the jungle, drawn on the Malayan Scouts, Ferret Force, the Australian SAS in Borneo and the Ranger jungle schools.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Airfield Seizure
concept: Parachute-capable raiding battalions that take an airfield by coup de main and open it for follow-on forces, from Entebbe and Kolwezi to the 75th Ranger Regiment at Grenada.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)
user_note: low contrast std 36

name: Army Commandos
concept: Small elite army units for direct action and sabotage, from the SAS in Malaya and Oman to Sayeret Matkal and the raids of the Six Day War.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Counter-Terror Assault Teams
concept: Dedicated hostage-rescue squadrons formed after Munich and Entebbe, from GSG 9 and the 1980 Princes Gate embassy storming to the US 1st SFOD-Delta founded in 1977.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Foreign Internal Defense
concept: A-Team style detachments that train, advise and fight alongside local partner forces, the US Special Forces model for unconventional warfare and counterinsurgency begun at Fort Bragg in 1952.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Sapper Infiltration
concept: Dac cong sappers who crawl through wire and strike airbases and headquarters with satchel charges and rockets, the Vietnamese and Korean infiltration tradition that peaked at Tet 1968.
archives: Commons "People's Liberation Army", "Vietnam People's Army"; NARA captured photos

name: Deep Sabotage and Decapitation
concept: Spetsnaz brigades formed from 1950 to find nuclear delivery means, headquarters and airfields in the enemy rear and destroy them in the opening hours of a war.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Stay-Behind Networks
concept: Cells of local volunteers with hidden arms, radios and caches meant to fight on behind an occupying army, from the British Auxiliary Units model to the NATO Gladio and Nordic stay-behind plans.
archives: DVIDS; NARA; Commons "United States Army in the Cold War", "Bundeswehr in the 1980s"; Bundesarchiv

name: Naval Commandos
concept: Combat swimmers and boat raiders for harbor penetration and coastal reconnaissance, the SBS, Italian Decima MAS successors and Israeli Shayetet 13.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Maritime Counter-Terror
concept: Teams trained to retake ships and offshore platforms, after the Achille Lauro and Munich, such as SEAL Team Six of 1980 and the SBS Maritime Counter-Terrorism squadron.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Underwater Demolition Teams
concept: Frogmen who survey beaches and clear obstacles ahead of landings, the US UDT of Korea and Vietnam and the Royal Navy clearance divers.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Swimmer Delivery Vehicles
concept: Midget submarines, wet subs and diver propulsion craft launched from mother submarines to attack naval bases, in the line of Italian human torpedoes and Soviet naval Spetsnaz.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Air Commandos
concept: Aircrew-integrated teams for combat control, pathfinding and deep insertion by air, from the Burma Air Commandos to the 1st Air Commando Group of 1961.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Combat Search and Rescue
concept: Pararescue jumpers and helicopter crews that recover downed pilots under fire, the Jolly Green and Sandy missions that saved thousands of aircrew in Vietnam.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Forward Air Controllers
concept: Combat controllers and Raven FACs that put air strikes onto targets in the jungle fight, the Vietnam model of Misty and Raven teams working with ground units.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Long Range Air Insertion
concept: Low level transport and gunship support for deep raids, the Son Tay prisoner camp raid of 1970, Entebbe flown by C-130 and the Soviet Il-76 airlift of special forces.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Legion Shock Troops
concept: Foreign Legion parachute and commando regiments used as a shock force, from Dien Bien Phu and Algeria to the 2nd REP jump on Kolwezi in 1978.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Legion Pacification Garrisons
concept: Legion companies in fortified posts that patrol and road-build to hold pacified territory, the Sahara and Djibouti garrisons and the Algerian quadrillage.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Regional Special Forces Groups
concept: Special forces split into region-focused groups with language and culture training and a long standing relation with allied partners, as the US Army did in the 1960s.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Unified Special Operations Command
concept: Single joint command over all special forces, created after the Desert One failure in 1980 and codified by the Nunn-Cohen amendment and the 1987 US Special Operations Command.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Ground-Controlled Interception
concept: Radar chains, filter rooms and controllers on the ground steer every interceptor onto its target. The fighter becomes the weapon of an air defence system, not a lone hunter.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Fighter Sweeps
concept: Large formations of fighters range ahead of the strike force to clear the sky and fight for air supremacy over the enemy's own airfields.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Missile Interceptors
concept: All-weather interceptors armed with radar-guided missiles trade manoeuvrability for the ability to kill bombers at long range, day or night.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Dissimilar Air Combat
concept: Pilots train against unlike aircraft and unlike tactics, learning to fight an enemy who flies a different machine and plays by different rules.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Beyond Visual Range Combat
concept: Look-down radar and active-guided missiles shift the fight to the first shot, taken before the enemy ever sees you.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Energy Maneuverability
concept: Fighter design and tactics are built around the management of energy: speed, altitude and turn rate traded against each other to win the close fight.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Cab Rank Close Support
concept: Fighter-bombers orbit over the front, called in by forward air controllers who direct them onto targets within minutes of the request.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Maritime Strike
concept: Torpedo, rocket and bomb-armed strike aircraft are trained to find and sink ships far from home, from land bases and carrier decks alike.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Interdiction Strike
concept: Strike aircraft go beyond the battle line to break roads, rail yards and depots, isolating the front from its supply.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Wild Weasel SEAD
concept: Specially equipped aircraft hunt radars and missile batteries, opening corridors through integrated air defences for the main strike.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Precision-Guided Strike
concept: Laser, television and satellite guidance turn one sortie into one destroyed target, and make strike aircraft effective at a fraction of the former sortie rate.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Tank Busting
concept: Cannon, rocket and guided-missile armed aircraft are built and trained to destroy massed armoured columns from the air.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Tactical Reconnaissance
concept: Photographic and visual reconnaissance aircraft give the army a current picture of the enemy and the air force a list of targets.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Light Bomber Interdiction
concept: Twin-engine light bombers carry the war to rail lines, depots and convoys behind the front in steady, repeated sorties.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Low-Level Penetration
concept: Tactical bombers fly under the radar horizon at treetop height, trading range and comfort for survival against modern air defence.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Electronic Countermeasures
concept: Jamming pods, chaff and electronic escorts blind and confuse the enemy's radars and missile guidance, protecting the strike package.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Airborne Early Warning
concept: Radar aircraft on station over the battlefield extend detection range and let a controller direct the entire air battle in real time.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Stealth Penetration
concept: Low-observable aircraft slip through defences that would destroy conventional strike packages, hitting the highest-value targets on the first night.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Strategic Air Command
concept: A centralised bomber force kept on constant readiness to deliver the nation's strategic strike, drilled until every crew knows its target.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Area Bombing
concept: Massed formations of heavy bombers flatten industrial districts and cities, accepting heavy losses to break the enemy's will and output.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Airborne Alert
concept: Part of the bomber force is always in the air, so that no first strike can catch the deterrent on the ground.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Maritime Patrol and ASW
concept: Long-range patrol aircraft quarter the ocean with radar, sonobuoys and depth weapons, hunting submarines from the air.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Standoff Cruise Missiles
concept: Bombers launch cruise missiles from beyond the reach of enemy defences, so the aircraft survives and the target does not.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Conventional Heavy Bombing
concept: The heavy bomber force is re-roled for sustained conventional campaigns, with precision weapons, huge payloads and enduring sortie rates.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Counter-Air Dominance
concept: Win the air by hunting the enemy fighter force wherever it flies. Aces, free-ranging sweeps and constant adversary training keep the kill ratio high.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Continental Air Defense
concept: All-weather interceptors on ground alert, tied to a continent-wide radar net, stand between the homeland and the bomber stream.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Frontal Aviation Air Cover
concept: Fighters belong to the front commander and fly where the armies advance, ground-controlled over an umbrella of missile belts.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Airfield Suppression Strikes
concept: A dawn blow on enemy runways wins the air war before it starts. Strike aircraft go low, deep and first.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Nuclear Strike Fighter-Bombers
concept: Fighter-bombers on quick-reaction alert carry tactical nuclear weapons toward targets across the front line. Range and release authority matter more than gun power.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Air-Land Close Support
concept: Air liaison officers, forward controllers and armored attack aircraft turn close support into an extension of the corps commander's fires.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Swing-Role Multirole
concept: One airframe, one wing, any mission. Multirole fighters shift from air superiority to strike in the same sortie cycle, and escort their own bombs.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Tactical Nuclear Bombers
concept: Canberras and Il-28s carry special weapons to the opposing airfields and ports. Night, low altitude and strict nuclear surety define the mission.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Frontal Bomber Aviation
concept: Medium bombers are assigned to the front and strike the enemy's second echelon, depots and command posts in the army's own operational timetable.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Aerial Refueling Network
concept: Tanker tracks and radar aircraft extend the reach of every wing. Air power moves with the fleet of tankers instead of waiting for forward bases.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Dispersed Alert Basing
concept: Bombers spread across dozens of fields so that no first strike can find them all. A fleet that survives is a fleet that deters.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)

name: Battlefield Heavy Bombardment
concept: Strategic bombers drop on ground-directed coordinates in front of the army. The heavy bomber becomes a flying artillery park.
archives: Commons, DVIDS, NARA (match subject)
